blocks.content: Chemical reactions are processes in which substances undergo chemical changes to form new substances with different properties. During a chemical reaction, atoms rearrange themselves to form new molecules. Chemical reactions are essential in everyday life, industrial processes and biological systems.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A chemical reaction involves the breaking and making of bonds between atoms to produce new substances with distinct chemical properties.
A balanced chemical equation must have an equal number of atoms of each element on both sides to satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass.
Key indicators of a chemical reaction include evolution of gas, change in color, change in temperature, and formation of a precipitate.
Oxidation is the addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen, whereas reduction involves the addition of hydrogen or removal of oxygen.
Corrosion damages metal structures through oxidation, while rancidity refers to the oxidation of fats and oils leading to spoiled food taste and odor.

blocks.content: • A chemical reaction is a process in which one or more substances are transformed into new substances.
• The substances that take part in a reaction are called reactants.
• The substances formed in a reaction are called products.
• Chemical reactions involve breaking and forming of chemical bonds.
A chemical equation is a symbolic representation of a chemical reaction using chemical formulas.
A balanced chemical equation has an equal number of atoms of each element on both sides.
Chemical reactions involve the breaking and making of bonds between atoms to produce new substances.
Oxidation: Addition of oxygen or loss of hydrogen.

blocks.content: Reduction: Removal of oxygen or gain of hydrogen.
These reactions together are called redox reactions.
Corrosion is the gradual destruction of metals due to chemical reactions with the environment. Rusting of iron is the most common example.
Rancidity refers to the oxidation of fats and oils in food which causes unpleasant smell and taste. It can be prevented by storing food in airtight containers.

items: Questions frequently test balancing chemical equations based on the Law of Conservation of Mass.
Differentiate clearly between displacement and double displacement reactions (precipitation reactions).
Redox reactions involve simultaneous oxidation and reduction; identify the oxidizing agent and reducing agent correctly in given reactions.
Preventive methods for corrosion (galvanization with zinc) and rancidity (flushing with nitrogen gas) are common objective-type questions.

blocks.content: A catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed in the reaction.
Examples: Platinum, Iron catalyst in Haber process
• Rusting of iron is a common example of corrosion.
• Redox reactions involve oxidation and reduction.
